『{{jalink|延喜式|Q1342448}}』{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932|神名帳}}における祭神の記載は1座。同帳では「木嶋坐天照御魂神社」と記載されるが、この社名は「木嶋（地名）に鎮座する天照御魂神の社」という意味であるため、本来は「'''天照御魂神'''（あまてるみむすびのかみ/あまてるみたまのかみ）」を祀った神社とされる。神名帳では、{{jalink|山城国|Q749276}}の木嶋社のほかにも{{jalink|大和国|Q907495}}・{{jalink|摂津国|Q864163}}・{{jalink|丹波国|Q954511}}・{{jalink|播磨国|Q1047523}}・{{jalink|対馬国|Q1054861}}などに天照御魂神・天照神・天照玉神を祀る祠の存在が見られるが、これらは{{jalink|天照大神|Q455602}}（皇祖神）とは別の神格の太陽神と考えられている{{jalink|松前健|Q11529297}} 『日本神話の謎がよく分かる本』 大和書房、2007年、pp. 42-43。。 木嶋社の天照御魂神の神格について、史料上では天照国照天火明命（{{jalink|天火明命|Q10940411}}）説・天照大神説・天日神命説などが見られる{{Sfn|木島坐天照御魂神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（神道大辞典）|1941}}。上記の天照御魂神・天照神・天照玉神を社名とする神社の多くでは現在の祭神が天火明命（{{jalink|尾張氏|Q11465311}}祖神）とされることに基づき、これらの神を特に尾張氏の奉斎神とする説があり、その説の中で木嶋社の地には元々尾張氏系の人々がいて天照御魂神を奉斎していたが、{{jalink|秦氏|Q987290}}の渡来・開拓とともにその在地系祭祀が継承されたと説明される{{jalink|水谷千秋|Q11549157}} 『謎の渡来人秦氏（文春新書734）』 文藝春秋、2009年、pp. 202-203。。また、『延喜式』神名帳に確認できる天照神のうち、{{jalink|尾張氏|Q11465311}}やその同族が祭祀に関与していたと考えられるのは、{{jalink|水主坐天照御魂神社}}・{{jalink|鏡作坐天照御魂神社|Q38278496}}・{{jalink|新屋坐天照御魂神社|Q11501968}}・{{jalink|天照玉命神社}}・{{jalink|粒坐天照神社|Q11604472}}の5社、{{jalink|対馬国|Q1054861|対馬氏}}らによって奉祀されていたと考えられるのが{{jalink|阿麻氐留神社|Q123118284}}1社で、残りの木嶋坐天照御魂神社・{{jalink|他田坐天照御魂神社|Q43594600}}・{{jalink|天照大神高座神社}}・{{jalink|伊勢天照御祖神社}}の4社については史料も乏しく確認ができないものの、木嶋社は{{jalink|阿麻氐留神社|Q123118284}}の祭神・{{jalink|天日神命|Q133505245}}のように、{{jalink|対馬国|Q1054861|対馬氏}}の祭祀した日神であったとする説もある北條勝貴「松尾大社における市杵嶋姫命の鎮座について」(『国立歴史民俗博物館研究報告』72集､1997年3月）。一方、木嶋社境内の{{jalink|三柱鳥居|Q3532297}}の方位が稲荷山・松尾山の冬至線、{{jalink|比叡山|Q748040}}四明岳・{{jalink|愛宕山 (京都市)|Q2975204|愛宕山}}の夏至線に関係すると見て、境内の元糺の池に日が差すという構造から、朝鮮半島の日光感精型の信仰に基づく半島系の太陽神（日の御子）とする説もある{{Sfn|木島坐天照御魂神社（神々）|1986}}。そのほか「ミムスビ」という神名から、境内の湧水によって穀物を生成する{{jalink|むすひ|Q11279555|ムスヒ}}の神とする説もある{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。 このように古代の祭神の神格は不詳ながら、{{jalink|1883年|Q7816}}（{{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}16年）の『葛野郡神社明細帳』では上記5柱の神名が記載されており、これらが現在まで継承されている{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。 === 歴史 === === 創建 === 創建は不詳{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。一説に、{{jalink|推古天皇|Q298057}}12年（{{jalink|604年|Q31048}}）に{{jalink|広隆寺|Q3076920}}創建に伴い{{jalink|勧請}}されたともいわれる{{Sfn|木嶋神社（平凡社）|1979}}{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|p=17}}。史料からは{{jalink|大宝 (日本)|Q1346269|大宝}}元年（{{jalink|701年|Q23496}}）の記事以前の祭祀の存在が認められている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。 前述（「{{jalink|#祭神||祭神}}」節）のように祭祀の淵源には諸説があるが、嵯峨野・太秦周辺は渡来系氏族の{{jalink|秦氏|Q987290}}が開拓した地で、{{jalink|広隆寺|Q3076920}}・{{jalink|松尾大社|Q710302}}・{{jalink|蛇塚古墳|Q11625508}}などの関係寺社・史跡が知られることから、木嶋社もまた秦氏ゆかりの神社といわれる{{Sfn|木嶋神社（平凡社）|1979}}。また現在本殿の東隣に鎮座する蚕養神社は、この秦氏が招来した養蚕・機織・染色技術に因むと推測される{{Sfn|蚕養神社（神々）|1986}}。ただし秦氏の渡来以前にも、木嶋社付近では和泉式部町遺跡などの{{jalink|弥生時代|Q207858}}頃からの集住を表す遺跡の存在が知られている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。 {{jalink|北條勝貴}}は、『{{jalink|日本書紀|Q813935}}』{{jalink|顕宗天皇|Q360966}}紀において、{{jalink|阿閉事代|Q57538465}}という同一人物の関与（コトシロは神の言葉を預かり述べる象徴的な人物を意味するとされる）や、事代に託宣を下すのが{{jalink|タカミムスビ||高皇産霊命}}を祖とする月神・日神であるという神格の対応性、祭祀を司る氏族がともに{{jalink|玄界灘|Q498047}}の島を本拠とし{{jalink|卜部|Q94724}}を出す壱岐・対馬の旧国造系氏族であるという祭祀担当者の対応性からすれば、壱岐・対馬の日神・月神が密接な関係にあることは明らかであり、木嶋社が元来対馬氏によって奉祀されていたのか、それとも{{jalink|尾張氏|Q11465311}}系の氏族によって奉祀されていたのかは不明であるが、顕宗3年2月紀・4月紀に見える、上記のような対応性を考慮すれば、日神を奉祀する木嶋社が葛野の{{jalink|月読神社 (京都市)|Q11516217|月読神社}}と地理的に近接している事実は無視できず、日月の両信仰が、ある時期に玄界灘から{{jalink|畿内|Q906708}}地方へともに移植され、両社もそれらと軌を一にして創建されたものではないかとしている北條勝貴「松尾大社における市杵嶋姫命の鎮座について」（『国立歴史民俗博物館研究報告』72集、1997年3月）。 === 概史 === {{jalink|六国史|Q1151168|国史}}での初見は『{{jalink|続日本紀|Q611399}}』{{jalink|大宝 (日本)|Q1346269|大宝}}元年（{{jalink|701年|Q23496}}）『続日本紀』大宝元年（701年）4月丙午（3日）条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。条で、{{jalink|山背国}}{{jalink|葛野郡|Q13579879}}の「木島神」のほか{{jalink|月読神社 (京都市)|Q11516217|月読神}}・{{jalink|水主神社 (城陽市)|Q54153262|樺井神}}・{{jalink|羽束師坐高御産日神社|Q65278999|波都賀志神}}の神稲を同年以後は{{jalink|中臣氏|Q1198447}}に給すると見える{{Sfn|木嶋神社（平凡社）|1979}}。 『{{jalink|新抄格勅符抄|Q11502312}}』{{jalink|大同 (日本)|Q1373191|大同}}元年（{{jalink|806年|Q30021}}）牒『新抄格勅符抄』巻10（神事諸家封戸）大同元年（806年）牒（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。によれば、当時の「許志摩神」には{{jalink|神戸 (民戸)|Q11589711|神戸}}として山城国から9戸が充てられていた{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。続けて国史では、{{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}3年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）1月には「木島天照御魂神」の{{jalink|神階|Q11591025}}が正五位下に昇叙された旨や、同年（{{jalink|貞観 (日本)|Q1075635|貞観}}元年）9月『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）9月8日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。・貞観17年（{{jalink|875年|Q23816}}）7月『日本三代実録』貞観17年（875年）7月2日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。・{{jalink|元慶|Q747451}}元年（{{jalink|877年|Q23905}}）6月『日本三代実録』元慶元年（877年）6月14日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。には雨乞のための奉幣、貞観17年8月『日本紀略』貞観17年（875年）8月25日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。には秋稔のための奉幣が遣わされた旨が記されているほか、元慶元年4月条『日本三代実録』元慶元年（877年）4月13日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。にも記載が見える{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|木島神社（角川）|1982}}。 {{jalink|延長 (元号)|Q1327274|延長}}5年（{{jalink|927年|Q30470}}）成立の『{{jalink|延喜式|Q1342448}}』{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932|神名帳}}では山城国葛野郡に「木島坐天照御魂神社 名神大 月次相嘗新嘗」として、{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}に列するとともに朝廷の{{jalink|月次祭|Q11516161}}・{{jalink|相嘗祭|Q11581944}}・{{jalink|新嘗祭|Q11501518}}では{{jalink|幣帛|Q11481885}}に預かった旨が記載されている{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。社名の読みは吉田家本で「アマテラスミムスヒ」、金剛寺本で「アマテルミムスヒ」と振られるが、後世の『{{jalink|神名帳考証|Q11588824}}』・『神祇志料』・『{{jalink|神社覈録|Q11590708}}』では「アマテルミタマ」とする{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。『延喜式』では、ほかに四時祭下 相嘗祭条、臨時祭 祈雨祭条、臨時祭 名神祭条においてもそれぞれ木嶋社の記載がある{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。 {{jalink|広隆寺|Q3076920}}の{{jalink|縁起|Q522046}}である『広隆寺来由記』（山城州葛野郡楓野大堰郷広隆寺来由記、{{jalink|明応|Q1193841}}8年（{{jalink|1499年|Q6708}}）成立）[{{NDLDC|1879799/384}} 『群書類従 新校 第十八巻』]（内外書籍、1931年-1937年、国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）384-388コマ。では、貞観年間（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}} - {{jalink|877年|Q23905}}）に僧の{{jalink|道昌|Q11367403}}が勅命により「木島名神」の池水に祈雨のため加持を行なった旨や、祈雨の神として崇敬されたことで神階が順次昇叙され{{jalink|長久|Q1193530}}4年（{{jalink|1043年|Q19348}}）に正一位の極位に達した旨が記載されているほか、延喜年間に広隆寺に勧請された鎮守38所のうちで「木島{{sub| 女。正一位}}」と女神として記載されている{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。{{jalink|平安時代|Q193292}}末期の『{{jalink|梁塵秘抄|Q3010584}}』では、木嶋社が{{jalink|伏見稲荷大社|Q714828}}や{{jalink|石清水八幡宮|Q710098}}と並んで参拝者が絶えず賑わった神社として歌われている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。 {{jalink|鎌倉時代|Q236205}}の{{jalink|承久|Q1195428}}3年（{{jalink|1221年|Q5393}}）の{{jalink|承久の乱|Q1372308}}では、『{{jalink|吾妻鏡|Q1042324}}』『吾妻鏡』承久3年（1221年）6月15日条。において{{jalink|後鳥羽天皇|Q316658|後鳥羽上皇}}側の{{jalink|三浦胤義|Q11356551}}と子の胤連、兼義が「西山木嶋」で自殺したと見えるが、これは当地に比定される{{Sfn|木嶋神社（平凡社）|1979}}。『{{jalink|承久記|Q11497315}}』によれば、胤義は「子の嶋と云ふ社」に隠れていたが末路を悟って自害し、郎従が社に火をかけたという{{Sfn|木嶋神社（平凡社）|1979}}。近年の境内発掘調査では、この焼失後の社殿再興時のものと見られる鎌倉時代前期頃の整地の跡が認められている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=14-16}}。 その後は{{jalink|江戸時代|Q184963}}頃まで文献に記載が見られず、変遷は不詳{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。{{jalink|安永}}9年（{{jalink|1780年|Q7716}}）の『{{jalink|都名所図会|Q11643495}}』では当時の境内の様子が描かれている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。 {{jalink|明治維新|Q8707}}後、{{jalink|1873年|Q7757}}（{{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}6年）6月に{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534}}において{{jalink|郷社|Q134917316}}に列した{{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912}}。 {{jalink|1985年|Q2431}}（{{jalink|昭和|Q327567}}60年）に境内は京都市指定史跡に指定された。{{jalink|2002年|Q1987}}（{{jalink|平成|Q234510}}14年）には、境内北東隅における消防用防火槽設置に伴い、史跡としての発掘調査が初めて実施されている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。 === 神階 === * 六国史時代における{{jalink|神階|Q11591025}}奉叙の記録 ** {{jalink|天安 (日本)|Q1075611|天安}}3年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）1月27日、従五位下から正五位下 （『{{jalink|日本三代実録|Q1052981}}』）『日本三代実録』貞観元年（859年）正月27日条（{{Harvnb|神道・神社史料集成}}参照）。 - 表記は「木島天照御魂神」。 * 六国史以後 ** {{jalink|承平 (日本)|Q1324874|承平}}6年（{{jalink|936年|Q23584}}）10月23日、正五位上から従四位下 （『広隆寺来由記』） ** {{jalink|長保|Q1324844}}5年（{{jalink|1003年|Q19224}}）10月28日、従一位 （『広隆寺来由記』） ** {{jalink|長久|Q1193530}}4年（{{jalink|1043年|Q19348}}）5月10日、正一位 （『広隆寺来由記』） === 境内 === [[File:Konoshima-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿（左）と蚕養神社（右）}}]] 境内は御室川右岸の低位段丘面上の東端にあり、{{jalink|双ヶ丘|Q18337635}}（双ヶ岡）の真南、{{jalink|広隆寺|Q3076920}}の真東に位置する{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。鳥居は、広隆寺の南門のほぼ真東にある{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。木嶋社は、その存在が文献上では古く{{jalink|大宝 (日本)|Q1346269|大宝}}元年（{{jalink|701年|Q23496}}）に見え、京都市内でも最古の神社の1つに位置づけられる。元糺の池の存在から文献上での祈雨記事との関連性がうかがえるほか、蚕養神社の存在から{{jalink|秦氏|Q987290}}との関連性が見られ、また巨樹の社叢から古来の姿がうかがえることから、境内は京都の歴史上重要な遺跡であるとして京都市指定史跡に指定されている[http://www.city.kyoto.jp/bunshi/bunkazai/siteisyasinn/sisekisetumei.htm#Anchor-31277 京都市指定・登録文化財 -史跡- > 木嶋坐天照御霊神社（蚕の社）境内]（京都市ホームページ）。。 社殿はいずれも明治以降の再興{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。本殿は境内の中央北寄りの、やや高所に建てられている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。本殿の東側には蚕養神社（こかいじんじゃ、東本殿）が鎮座し、「蚕の社」の通称は同社に由来する。これらの前に拝所・拝殿がある。 [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|元糺の池と{{jalink|三柱鳥居|Q3532297}}}}]] 境内の北西隅には「元糺の池（もとただすのいけ）」と称する神泉があり、現在は涸れているがかつては湧水が豊富であったといい、現在も夏の土用の丑の日にこの泉に手足を浸すと諸病に良いとして信仰されている{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。伝承では木嶋社の社叢を「元糺の森」、神泉を「元糺の池」と称し、{{jalink|下鴨神社}}の森が「{{jalink|糺の森|Q5359359}}」と呼ばれるようになる以前、元々は木嶋社の社叢が「糺の森」と呼ばれていたとする{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|p=17}}。 この元糺の池の中には'''{{jalink|三柱鳥居|Q3532297}}'''（みはしらとりい、三ツ鳥居/三面鳥居/三角鳥居）が建てられている{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}。これは柱3本を三角形に組み、3方から中心の神座を拝することを可能とする珍しい形式の{{jalink|鳥居|Q234731}}で{{Sfn|木嶋坐天照御魂神社（式内社）|1979}}、「京都三鳥居」の1つに数えられる「京都三鳥居」は、木嶋神社の三柱鳥居、{{jalink|京都御苑|Q843854}}の{{jalink|厳島神社 (京都市上京区)|Q11410134|厳島神社}}の唐破風鳥居、{{jalink|北野天満宮|Q662176}}境内社の伴氏社の石造鳥居の3基。。中央の神座は、円錐形に小石を積み、中心に御幣を立てて{{jalink|依代}}としたものである{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。この鳥居の起源等は詳らかでなく、秦氏の聖地である{{jalink|双ヶ丘|Q18337635}}・松尾山（{{jalink|松尾大社|Q710302}}神体山）・稲荷山（{{jalink|伏見稲荷大社|Q714828}}神体山）の遥拝方位を表したとする説などがある{{Sfn|木島坐天照御魂神社（神々）|1986}}三柱鳥居に関しては、{{jalink|キリスト教|Q5043}}{{jalink|ネストリウス派|Q168414}}の{{jalink|景教|Q13417194}}の遺跡であって秦氏が景教を将来したとする俗説もあったが、そもそもの景教の中国移入は635年、正式認可は638年であり、秦氏の渡来時期からかなり下るため否定されている {{Harv|木島坐天照御魂神社（神々）|1986}}。。現在の鳥居は{{jalink|天保|Q1369045}}2年（{{jalink|1831年|Q7579}}）の再興であるが{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}（社伝では{{jalink|享保|Q1145048}}年間（{{jalink|1716年|Q6892}} - {{jalink|1735年|Q6984}}）の修復{{Sfn|木嶋神社（平凡社）|1979}}）、{{jalink|安永}}9年（{{jalink|1780年|Q7716}}）の『{{jalink|都名所図会|Q11643495}}』では豊かな湧水とともに現在に見るのと同じ三柱鳥居の様子が描かれている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=3-5}}。 {{jalink|2002年|Q1987}}（{{jalink|平成|Q234510}}14年）の発掘調査によって、かつては本殿東側の各所にも泉のあったことが判明しており、元糺の池もそのような泉の1つが神聖化されたものと考えられている{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=14-16}}。この発掘調査では、少なくとも平安時代中期頃に遡る、泉に伴う石敷遺構が出土している{{Sfn|発掘調査報告書|2002|pp=14-16}}。 It is {{jalink|Shikiuchi}} ({{jalink|Meishin Taisha|Q9610964}}), and {{jalink|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534|Old shrine rank}} is {{jalink|Gosha|Q134917316}}. It is also commonly known as ``Konoshima Shrine'' (Konoshima Shrine) and ``Kaikono Yashiro'' (Silkworm Shrine). The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} 1st year ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{jalink|Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{jalink|Shimogamo Shrine}} is called "{{jalink|Tadasu no Mori|Q53593 59}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{jalink|Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. The current torii was rebuilt in {{jalink|Tenpo|Q1369045}}2 years ({{jalink|1831|Q7579}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{jalink|Kyoho|Q1145048}} years ({{jalink|1716|Q6892}} - {{jalink|1735|Q6984}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{jalink|Yasunaga}}9 ({{jalink|1780|Q7716}}) ``{{jalink|Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{jalink|2002|Q1987}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. "New Edition of Japanese Classical Literature Complete Works 42 Kagura Uta/Jimagaku/Ryojin Hisho/Kanginshu" Shogakukan, 2000 (Japan Knowledge Edition), p. 254. }} {{Cquote|The medicine man of Uzumasa keeps staying with Maro as he goes to his home.'''The God of Kijima''

In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{jalink|Yamashiro Province|Q749276}}, there are also {{jalink|Yamato Province|Q907495}}, {{jalink|Settsu Province|Q864163}}, {{jalink|Tamba Province|Q954511}}, {{jalink|Harima Province|Q1047523}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602}} (King Ancestor God){{jalink|Ken Matsumae|Q11529297}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{jalink|Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{jalink|Musuhi|Q11279555|Musuhi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{jalink|1883|Q7816}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{jalink|Emperor Suiko|Q298057}}12 ({{jalink|604|Q31048}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{jalink|requested}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{jalink|#enshrined deity||enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, an immigrant clan, and {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{jalink|Matsuo Taisha|Q710302}} and {{jalink|Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{jalink|Katsuki Hojo}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{jalink|Akojidai|Q57538465}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{jalink|Takamimusubi||Takōsanreimyo}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{jalink|Urabe|Q94724}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. In , it appears that {{jalink|Emperor Gotoba|Q316658|Retired Emperor Gotoba}}'s {{jalink|Taneyoshi Miura|Q11356551}} and his children Tanenren and Kaneyoshi committed suicide at ``Nishiyama Kijima'', but this is believed to be the place {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. According to ``{{jalink|Jōkyūki|Q11497315}}'', Taneyoshi was hiding in ``Konojima Shrine'', but when he realized his fate, he committed suicide, and Rojo set the shrine on fire {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Recent excavations within the shrine grounds have revealed traces of land leveling in the early Kamakura period, which appears to have been done during the rebuilding of the shrine building after it was destroyed by fire.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} After that, it is not mentioned in literature until around {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, and its history is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. {{jalink|Yasunaga}}9 ({{jalink|1780|Q7716}})'s ``{{jalink|Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495}}'' depicts the precincts at that time {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.After {{jalink|Meiji Restoration|Q8707}}, in June {{jalink|1873|Q7757}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}6) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{jalink|Gosha|Q134917316}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. In {{jalink|1985|Q2431}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}60), the precincts were designated as a designated historic site by Kyoto City . In {{jalink|2002|Q1987}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}14), an excavation survey was conducted for the first time as a historic site in conjunction with the installation of a fire tank in the northeast corner of the precincts.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. === God level === * Record of {{jalink|Divine rank|Q11591025}} dedication during the Six Kingdoms historical period ** {{jalink|Ten'an (Japan)|Q1075611|Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}), from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Sei Fifth Rank Lower ("{{jalink|Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981}}") "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" Article dated 27th New Year, Jogan 1st year (859) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). - The notation is "Kijima Amaterasu Mitama-kami." * After Six Kingdoms History ** {{jalink|Johei (Japan)|Q1324874|Johei}} October 23, 6th year ({{jalink|936|Q23584}}), from upper fifth rank to lower rank of junior fourth rank (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** October 28, {{jalink|Nagayasu|Q1324844}}5th year ({{jalink|1003|Q19224}}), Junichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** May 10th, {{jalink|Nagakyu|Q1193530}}4th year ({{jalink|1043|Q19348}}), Shoichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) === Precincts === [[File:Konoshima-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (left) and Seriyo Shrine (right)}}]] The precincts are located at the eastern end of the low terrace on the right bank of the Omuro River, just south of {{jalink|Futagaoka|Q18337635}} (Futagaoka) and just east of {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920}}. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} 1st year ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{jalink|Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{jalink|Shimogamo Shrine}} is called "{{jalink|Tadasu no Mori|Q53593 59}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{jalink|Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{jalink|Torii|Q234731}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{jalink|Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854}} {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|Itsukushima Shrine}}'s Karahafu torii, {{jalink|Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{jalink|Yorishiro}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{jalink|Futagaoka|Q18337635}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{jalink|Matsuo Taisha|Q710302}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{jalink|Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{jalink|Christianity|Q5043}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{jalink|Nestorian|Q168414}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. . The current torii was rebuilt in {{jalink|Tenpo|Q1369045}}2 years ({{jalink|1831|Q7579}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{jalink|Kyoho|Q1145048}} years ({{jalink|1716|Q6892}} - {{jalink|1735|Q6984}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{jalink|Yasunaga}}9 ({{jalink|1780|Q7716}}) ``{{jalink|Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{jalink|2002|Q1987}} ({{jalink|Heisei|Q234510}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. The common name of Kijima Shrine, ``Silkworm Shrine,'' originates from this Seriyo Shrine. * Akina Shrine *: Enshrined deity: Mitsui Takayasu ({{jalink|Mitsui family|Q950465}} distant ancestor) {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}} * Inari Shrine * Ryodo Shrine * Konchin Shrine * Misono Inari Shrine * Yasaka Shrine *Shokukuni Shrine * Tenma Shrine * Sanjuhachisho Shrine * Hakusei Shrine * Hakutoku Shrine * Hashihime Shrine * Tsubakioka Shrine === Cultural assets === === Kyoto City designated historic site === * Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts - Designated June 1, 1985 [http://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/bunshi/page/0000005897.html Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Property -Historic Site- Ukyo Ward] (Kyoto City Home Page). . === Appeared works === * 2 poems from “{{jalink|Ryojin Hisho|Q3010584}}” Volume 2 {{Cquote|Kane no Mitake is one place in the world, Kongo Zao Shaka Miroku, Inari, Yawata, Kijima, etc. There is no time when no one visits.
"New Edition of Japanese Classical Literature Complete Works 42 Kagura Uta/Jimagaku/Ryojin Hisho/Kanginshu" Shogakukan, 2000 (Japan Knowledge Edition), p. 254. }} {{Cquote|The medicine man of Uzumasa keeps staying with Maro as he goes to his home.'''The God of Kijima''
　{{small|Note) The medicine man of Uzumasa: Is it the Medicine Buddha of {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920}}?}}|20px||``Ryojin Hisho'' Volume 2 Two-Phrase Divine Poem Shrine Songs (No. 555) "New Complete Works of Japanese Classical Literature 42 Kagura Songs/Jimagaku/Ryojin Hisho/Kanginshu" Shogakukan, 2000 (Japan Knowledge Edition), p. 332. }} === Local information === '''Location''' * {{jalink|Kyoto In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{jalink|Yamashiro Province|Q749276}}, there are also {{jalink|Yamato Province|Q907495}}, {{jalink|Settsu Province|Q864163}}, {{jalink|Tamba Province|Q954511}}, {{jalink|Harima Province|Q1047523}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602}} (King Ancestor God){{jalink|Ken Matsumae|Q11529297}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{jalink|Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{jalink|Owari clan|Q11465311}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{jalink|Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{jalink|Owari clan|Q11465311}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{jalink|Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine}}・{{jalink|Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496}}・{{jalink|Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine |Q11501968}}, {{jalink|Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine}}, {{jalink|Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472}}, {{jalink| There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|Tsushima clan}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. On the other hand, the direction of the {{jalink|three pillar torii|Q3532297}} in the grounds of Kijima Shrine is the winter solstice line of Mt. Inari and Mt. Matsuo, and the direction of Mt. Shimeidake and Mt. Atago. (Kyoto City)|Q2975204|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} is believed to be related to the summer solstice line of Mt. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{jalink|Musuhi|Q11279555|Musuhi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{jalink|1883|Q7816}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{jalink|Emperor Suiko|Q298057}}12 ({{jalink|604|Q31048}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{jalink|requested}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{jalink|#enshrined deity||enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, an immigrant clan, and {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{jalink|Matsuo Taisha|Q710302}} and {{jalink|Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{jalink|Katsuki Hojo}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{jalink|Akojidai|Q57538465}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{jalink|Takamimusubi||Takōsanreimyo}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{jalink|Urabe|Q94724}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{jalink|Owari clan|Q11465311}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{jalink|Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno. According to ``{{jalink|Jōkyūki|Q11497315}}'', Taneyoshi was hiding in ``Konojima Shrine'', but when he realized his fate, he committed suicide, and Rojo set the shrine on fire {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Recent excavations within the shrine grounds have revealed traces of land leveling in the early Kamakura period, which appears to have been done during the rebuilding of the shrine building after it was destroyed by fire.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} After that, it is not mentioned in literature until around {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}}, and its history is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. {{jalink|Yasunaga}}9 ({{jalink|1780|Q7716}})'s ``{{jalink|Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495}}'' depicts the precincts at that time {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.After {{jalink|Meiji Restoration|Q8707}}, in June {{jalink|1873|Q7757}} ({{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}6) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{jalink|Gosha|Q134917316}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} 1st year ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{jalink|Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{jalink|Shimogamo Shrine}} is called "{{jalink|Tadasu no Mori|Q53593 59}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{jalink|Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{jalink|Torii|Q234731}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{jalink|Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854}} {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|Itsukushima Shrine}}'s Karahafu torii, {{jalink|Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{jalink|Yorishiro}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{jalink|Futagaoka|Q18337635}}, Mt. It is {{jalink|Shikiuchi}} ({{jalink|Meishin Taisha|Q9610964}}), and {{jalink|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534|Old shrine rank}} is {{jalink|Gosha|Q134917316}}. It is also commonly known as ``Konoshima Shrine'' (Konoshima Shrine) and ``Kaikono Yashiro'' (Silkworm Shrine). This shrine has long been worshiped as the god of prayers for rain, and is known for having a rare {{jalink|three-pillar torii|Q3532297}} within its grounds. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . :* {{jalink|Amenominakanushikami|Q2842779}} :* {{jalink|Okuni Tamakami}} :* {{jalink|Hoori|Q1051960|Hodemi Mikoto}} :* {{jalink|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|Ugayafukiaezu Mikoto}} :* {{jalink|Ninigi|Q1056017|Keorigi no Mikoto}} (Ninigi no Mikoto) {{Location map+|Japan|width=220|float=right|caption={{Center|Distribution of Amaterasu Mitama Shrine, Amaterasu Shrine, and
Amaterasu Tama no Mikoto Shrine}}|places= {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=53.49|lon_deg=135|lon_min=42|lon_sec=48.71|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=50|lat_sec=36.27|lon_deg=135|lon_min=45|lon_sec=42.43|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}}{{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=32|lat_sec=45.87|lon_deg=135|lon_min=50|lon_sec=21.08|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=33|lat_sec=41.59|lon_deg=135|lon_min=47|lon_sec=38.68|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=50|lat_sec=48.60|lon_deg=135|lon_min=32|lon_sec=57.81|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=36|lat_sec=44.79|lon_deg=135|lon_min=38|lon_sec=24.75|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=35|lat_min=17|lat_sec=51.46|lon_deg=135|lon_min=5|lon_sec=28.88|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}}{{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=51|lat_sec=49.25|lon_deg=134|lon_min=32|lon_sec=25.11|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=33|lat_min=19|lat_sec=0.06|lon_deg=130|lon_min=29|lon_sec=51.21|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=34|lat_min=20|lat_sec=23.47|lon_deg=129|lon_min=21|lon_sec=44.58|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=5}} }}In "{{jalink|Engishiki|Q1342448}}" {{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|Shinmyocho}}, there is one enshrined deity. In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{jalink|Yamashiro Province|Q749276}}, there are also {{jalink|Yamato Province|Q907495}}, {{jalink|Settsu Province|Q864163}}, {{jalink|Tamba Province|Q954511}}, {{jalink|Harima Province|Q1047523}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602}} (King Ancestor God){{jalink|Ken Matsumae|Q11529297}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{jalink|Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{jalink|Owari clan|Q11465311}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{jalink|Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{jalink|Owari clan|Q11465311}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{jalink|Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine}}・{{jalink|Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496}}・{{jalink|Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine |Q11501968}}, {{jalink|Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine}}, {{jalink|Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472}}, {{jalink| There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|Tsushima clan}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. One theory is that in {{jalink|Emperor Suiko|Q298057}}12 ({{jalink|604|Q31048}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{jalink|requested}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{jalink|#enshrined deity||enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, an immigrant clan, and {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{jalink|Matsuo Taisha|Q710302}} and {{jalink|Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{jalink|Yayoi period|Q207858}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{jalink|Katsuki Hojo}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{jalink|Akojidai|Q57538465}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{jalink|Takamimusubi||Takōsanreimyo}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} 1st year ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{jalink|Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{jalink|Shimogamo Shrine}} is called "{{jalink|Tadasu no Mori|Q53593 59}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{jalink|Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{jalink|Torii|Q234731}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{jalink|Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854}} {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|Itsukushima Shrine}}'s Karahafu torii, {{jalink|Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{jalink|Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|Taiho}} 1st year ({{jalink|701|Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{jalink|Hata clan|Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{jalink|Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{jalink|Shimogamo Shrine}} is called "{{jalink|Tadasu no Mori|Q53593 59}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{jalink|Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{jalink|Torii|Q234731}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{jalink|Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854}} {{jalink|Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|Itsukushima Shrine}}'s Karahafu torii, {{jalink|Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{ill|lt=Yamashiro Province|Q749276|WD=Q749276}}, there are also {{ill|lt=Yamato Province|Q907495|WD=Q907495}}, {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|WD=Q864163}}, {{ill|lt=Tamba Province|Q954511|WD=Q954511}}, {{ill|lt=Harima Province|Q1047523|WD=Q1047523}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602}} (King Ancestor God){{ill|lt=Ken Matsumae|Q11529297|WD=Q11529297}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411|WD=Q10940411}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{ill|lt=Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|WD=Q11549157}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{ill||lt=Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496|WD=Q38278496}}・{{ill|lt=Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q11501968|WD=Q11501968}}, {{ill||lt=Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine|UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472|WD=Q11604472}}, {{ill|lt=There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|WD=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill||lt=requested|UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity||WD=|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill||lt=Katsuki Hojo|UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|lt=Takamimusubi||WD=|lt=Takōsanreimyo}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|lt=Urabe|Q94724|WD=Q94724}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno. (Kyoto City)|Q11516217|WD=Q11516217|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine}} cannot be ignored. In "Engishiki," Kijima Shrine is also mentioned in the Shijisai Shita Ainosaijo, the Extraordinary Festival Prayer Festival, and the Extraordinary Festival Meishinsaijo."Koryuji Raiyuki" which is {{ill|lt=Engage|Q522046|WD=Q522046}} of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920}} (Koryuji Raiyuki, Kaedeno Oigo, Kadeno Oigo, Kazuno District, Yamashiro Prefecture, established in {{ill|lt=Meio|Q1193841|WD=Q1193841}} 8 ({{ill|lt=1499|Q6708|WD=Q6708}})) [{{NDLDC|1879799/384}} "Gunshoju Shinkyo Volume 18"] (Naigai Publishing, 1931-1937, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 384-388 frames. In the Jogan era ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897}} - In {{ill|lt=877|Q23905|WD=Q23905}}), the monk {{ill|lt=Dosho|Q11367403|WD=Q11367403}} performed blessings for rain at the pond of Kijima Meishin by imperial order, and was revered as the god of rain, so he was successively promoted to the divine rank. It is written that he reached the highest rank of Shoichii in {{ill|lt=Nagakyu|Q1193530|WD=Q1193530}}4 ({{ill|lt=1043|Q19348|WD=Q19348}}), and it is said that Kijima {{sub| {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292}} "{{ill|lt=Ryojin Hisho|Q3010584|WD=Q3010584}}", Kijima Shrine is {{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828}} and {{ill|lt=Iwashimizu Hachimangu Shrine|Q710098|WD=Q710098}}, it is said to be a shrine that was constantly crowded with worshipers. {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.In {{ill|lt=Jokyu War|Q1372308|WD=Q1372308}} of {{ill|lt=Jokyu|Q1195428|WD=Q1195428}} 3rd year ({{ill|lt=1221|Q5393|WD=Q5393}}) of {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|WD=Q236205}}, "{{ill|lt=Azuma Kagami|Q1042324|WD=Q1042324}}" Azuma Kagami article dated June 15, 1221. In , it appears that {{ill|lt=Emperor Gotoba|Q316658|WD=Q316658|lt=Retired Emperor Gotoba}}'s {{ill|lt=Taneyoshi Miura|Q11356551|WD=Q11356551}} and his children Tanenren and Kaneyoshi committed suicide at ``Nishiyama Kijima'', but this is believed to be the place {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. According to ``{{ill|lt=Jōkyūki|Q11497315|WD=Q11497315}}'', Taneyoshi was hiding in ``Konojima Shrine'', but when he realized his fate, he committed suicide, and Rojo set the shrine on fire {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Recent excavations within the shrine grounds have revealed traces of land leveling in the early Kamakura period, which appears to have been done during the rebuilding of the shrine building after it was destroyed by fire.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} After that, it is not mentioned in literature until around {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963}}, and its history is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. {{ill||lt=Yasunaga|UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716}})'s ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495}}'' depicts the precincts at that time {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.After {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707}}, in June {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}}6) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{ill|lt=Gosha|Q134917316|WD=Q134917316}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. In {{ill|lt=1985|Q2431|WD=Q2431}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567}}60), the precincts were designated as a designated historic site by Kyoto City . In {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510}}14), an excavation survey was conducted for the first time as a historic site in conjunction with the installation of a fire tank in the northeast corner of the precincts.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. === God level === * Record of {{ill|lt=Divine rank|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025}} dedication during the Six Kingdoms historical period ** {{ill|lt=Ten'an (Japan)|Q1075611|WD=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897}}), from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Sei Fifth Rank Lower ("{{ill|lt=Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981}}") "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" Article dated 27th New Year, Jogan 1st year (859) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). - The notation is "Kijima Amaterasu Mitama-kami." * After Six Kingdoms History ** {{ill|lt=Johei (Japan)|Q1324874|WD=Q1324874|lt=Johei}} October 23, 6th year ({{ill|lt=936|Q23584|WD=Q23584}}), from upper fifth rank to lower rank of junior fourth rank (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** October 28, {{ill|lt=Nagayasu|Q1324844|WD=Q1324844}}5th year ({{ill|lt=1003|Q19224|WD=Q19224}}), Junichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** May 10th, {{ill|lt=Nagakyu|Q1193530|WD=Q1193530}}4th year ({{ill|lt=1043|Q19348|WD=Q19348}}), Shoichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) === Precincts === [[File:Konoshima-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (left) and Seriyo Shrine (right)}}]] The precincts are located at the eastern end of the low terrace on the right bank of the Omuro River, just south of {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635}} (Futagaoka) and just east of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920}}. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill||lt=Shimogamo Shrine|UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill||lt=Tadasu no Mori|UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|lt=Torii|Q234731|WD=Q234731}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|lt=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|WD=Q843854}} {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|WD=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176|WD=Q662176}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{ill||lt=Yorishiro|UNKNOWN}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{ill|lt=Christianity|Q5043|WD=Q5043}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{ill|lt=Nestorian|Q168414|WD=Q168414}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. . The current torii was rebuilt in {{ill|lt=Tenpo|Q1369045|WD=Q1369045}}2 years ({{ill|lt=1831|Q7579|WD=Q7579}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048}} years ({{ill|lt=1716|Q6892|WD=Q6892}} - {{ill|lt=1735|Q6984|WD=Q6984}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{ill||lt=Yasunaga|UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716}}) ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. It is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikiuchi|UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=Meishin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964}}), and {{ill|lt=Modern shrine rank system|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|lt=Gosha|Q134917316|WD=Q134917316}}. It is also commonly known as ``Konoshima Shrine'' (Konoshima Shrine) and ``Kaikono Yashiro'' (Silkworm Shrine). This shrine has long been worshiped as the god of prayers for rain, and is known for having a rare {{ill|lt=three-pillar torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297}} within its grounds. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . :* {{ill|lt=Amenominakanushikami|Q2842779|WD=Q2842779}} :* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okuni Tamakami|UNKNOWN}} :* {{ill|lt=Hoori|Q1051960|WD=Q1051960|lt=Hodemi Mikoto}} :* {{ill|lt=Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|WD=Q1373935|lt=Ugayafukiaezu Mikoto}} :* {{ill|lt=Ninigi|Q1056017|WD=Q1056017|lt=Keorigi no Mikoto}} (Ninigi no Mikoto) {{Location map+|Japan|width=220|float=right|caption={{Center|Distribution of Amaterasu Mitama Shrine, Amaterasu Shrine, and

In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{ill|lt=Yamashiro Province|Q749276|WD=Q749276}}, there are also {{ill|lt=Yamato Province|Q907495|WD=Q907495}}, {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|WD=Q864163}}, {{ill|lt=Tamba Province|Q954511|WD=Q954511}}, {{ill|lt=Harima Province|Q1047523|WD=Q1047523}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602}} (King Ancestor God){{ill|lt=Ken Matsumae|Q11529297|WD=Q11529297}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411|WD=Q10940411}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{ill|lt=Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|WD=Q11549157}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine|UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori|UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity||WD=|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|lt=Takamimusubi||WD=|lt=Takōsanreimyo}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|lt=Urabe|Q94724|WD=Q94724}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno.
