In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{ill|lt=Yamashiro Province|Q749276|WD=Q749276|1=Yamashiro Province}}, there are also {{ill|lt=Yamato Province|Q907495|WD=Q907495|1=Yamato Province}}, {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|WD=Q864163|1=Settsu Province}}, {{ill|lt=Tamba Province|Q954511|WD=Q954511|1=Tanba Province}}, {{ill|lt=Harima Province|Q1047523|WD=Q1047523|1=Harima Province}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} (King Ancestor God){{ill|lt=Ken Matsumae|Q11529297|WD=Q11529297|1=Takeshi Matsumae}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411|WD=Q10940411|1=Amenohoakari}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{ill|lt=Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|WD=Q11549157|1=Chiaki Mizutani}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496|WD=Q38278496|1=Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}・{{ill|lt=Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q11501968|WD=Q11501968|1=Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472|WD=Q11604472|1=Iibo Nimasu Amaterasu Shrine}}, {{ill|lt=There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|WD=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan|1=Tsushima Province}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. On the other hand, the direction of the {{ill|lt=three pillar torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}} in the grounds of Kijima Shrine is the winter solstice line of Mt. Inari and Mt. Matsuo, and the direction of Mt. Shimeidake and Mt. Atago. (Kyoto City)|Q2975204|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} is believed to be related to the summer solstice line of Mt. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi|1=Musubi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816|1=1883}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048|1=604}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508|1=Hebizuka Kofun}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465|1=Akojidai}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|WD=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsanreimyo|1=Takamimusubi}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|lt=Urabe|Q94724|WD=Q94724|1=Radical 25}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno. (Kyoto City)|Q11516217|WD=Q11516217|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine|1=Tsukiyomi Shrine (Kyoto)}} cannot be ignored. The company's name is pronounced as "Amaterasu Mimusuhi" in the Yoshida family book and "Amateru Mimusuhi" in the Kongoji book, but later in the ``{{ill|lt=Shinmyocho kosho|Q11588824|WD=Q11588824|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies}}''・In ``Jingishiryo'' and ``{{ill|lt=Shinja Roku|Q11590708|WD=Q11590708|1=Jinja Kakuroku}}'', it is called ``Amateru Mitama''{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In "Engishiki," Kijima Shrine is also mentioned in the Shijisai Shita Ainosaijo, the Extraordinary Festival Prayer Festival, and the Extraordinary Festival Meishinsaijo."Koryuji Raiyuki" which is {{ill|lt=Engage|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}} (Koryuji Raiyuki, Kaedeno Oigo, Kadeno Oigo, Kazuno District, Yamashiro Prefecture, established in {{ill|lt=Meio|Q1193841|WD=Q1193841|1=Meiō}} 8 ({{ill|lt=1499|Q6708|WD=Q6708|1=1499}})) [{{NDLDC|1879799/384}} "Gunshoju Shinkyo Volume 18"] (Naigai Publishing, 1931-1937, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 384-388 frames. In the Jogan era ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}} - In {{ill|lt=877|Q23905|WD=Q23905|1=877}}), the monk {{ill|lt=Dosho|Q11367403|WD=Q11367403|1=Dōshō}} performed blessings for rain at the pond of Kijima Meishin by imperial order, and was revered as the god of rain, so he was successively promoted to the divine rank. It is written that he reached the highest rank of Shoichii in {{ill|lt=Nagakyu|Q1193530|WD=Q1193530|1=Chōkyū}}4 ({{ill|lt=1043|Q19348|WD=Q19348|1=1043}}), and it is said that Kijima {{sub| {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}} "{{ill|lt=Ryojin Hisho|Q3010584|WD=Q3010584|1=Ryōjin Hishō}}", Kijima Shrine is {{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828|1=Fushimi Inari-taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Iwashimizu Hachimangu Shrine|Q710098|WD=Q710098|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}, it is said to be a shrine that was constantly crowded with worshipers. {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.In {{ill|lt=Jokyu War|Q1372308|WD=Q1372308|1=Jōkyū War}} of {{ill|lt=Jokyu|Q1195428|WD=Q1195428|1=Jōkyū}} 3rd year ({{ill|lt=1221|Q5393|WD=Q5393|1=1221}}) of {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|WD=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}, "{{ill|lt=Azuma Kagami|Q1042324|WD=Q1042324|1=Azuma Kagami}}" Azuma Kagami article dated June 15, 1221. In , it appears that {{ill|lt=Emperor Gotoba|Q316658|WD=Q316658|lt=Retired Emperor Gotoba|1=Emperor Go-Toba}}'s {{ill|lt=Taneyoshi Miura|Q11356551|WD=Q11356551|1=Miura Taneyoshi}} and his children Tanenren and Kaneyoshi committed suicide at ``Nishiyama Kijima'', but this is believed to be the place {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. According to ``{{ill|lt=Jōkyūki|Q11497315|WD=Q11497315|1=Jōkyūki}}'', Taneyoshi was hiding in ``Konojima Shrine'', but when he realized his fate, he committed suicide, and Rojo set the shrine on fire {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Recent excavations within the shrine grounds have revealed traces of land leveling in the early Kamakura period, which appears to have been done during the rebuilding of the shrine building after it was destroyed by fire.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} After that, it is not mentioned in literature until around {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, and its history is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716|1=1780}})'s ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495|1=Miyako meisho zue}}'' depicts the precincts at that time {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.After {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707|1=Meiji Restoration}}, in June {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757|1=1873}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}6) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{ill|lt=Gosha|Q134917316|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. In {{ill|lt=1985|Q2431|WD=Q2431|1=1985}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}60), the precincts were designated as a designated historic site by Kyoto City . In {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987|1=2002}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}14), an excavation survey was conducted for the first time as a historic site in conjunction with the installation of a fire tank in the northeast corner of the precincts.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. === God level === * Record of {{ill|lt=Divine rank|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025|1=Shinkai (divine rank)}} dedication during the Six Kingdoms historical period ** {{ill|lt=Ten'an (Japan)|Q1075611|WD=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an|1=Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}}), from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Sei Fifth Rank Lower ("{{ill|lt=Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}") "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" Article dated 27th New Year, Jogan 1st year (859) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). - The notation is "Kijima Amaterasu Mitama-kami." * After Six Kingdoms History ** {{ill|lt=Johei (Japan)|Q1324874|WD=Q1324874|lt=Johei|1=Jōhei}} October 23, 6th year ({{ill|lt=936|Q23584|WD=Q23584|1=936}}), from upper fifth rank to lower rank of junior fourth rank (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** October 28, {{ill|lt=Nagayasu|Q1324844|WD=Q1324844|1=Chōhō (era)}}5th year ({{ill|lt=1003|Q19224|WD=Q19224|1=1003}}), Junichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** May 10th, {{ill|lt=Nagakyu|Q1193530|WD=Q1193530|1=Chōkyū}}4th year ({{ill|lt=1043|Q19348|WD=Q19348|1=1043}}), Shoichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) === Precincts === [[File:Konoshima-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (left) and Seriyo Shrine (right)}}]] The precincts are located at the eastern end of the low terrace on the right bank of the Omuro River, just south of {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635|1=Narabigaoka}} (Futagaoka) and just east of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori|1=UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|lt=Torii|Q234731|WD=Q234731|1=Torii}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|lt=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|WD=Q843854|1=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden}} {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|WD=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine (Kyoto)}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176|WD=Q662176|1=Kitano Tenmangū}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yorishiro|1=UNKNOWN}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635|1=Narabigaoka}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828|1=Fushimi Inari-taisha}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{ill|lt=Christianity|Q5043|WD=Q5043|1=Christianity}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{ill|lt=Nestorian|Q168414|WD=Q168414|1=Nestorianism}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. . The current torii was rebuilt in {{ill|lt=Tenpo|Q1369045|WD=Q1369045|1=Tenpō}}2 years ({{ill|lt=1831|Q7579|WD=Q7579|1=1831}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}} years ({{ill|lt=1716|Q6892|WD=Q6892|1=1716}} - {{ill|lt=1735|Q6984|WD=Q6984|1=1735}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716|1=1780}}) ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495|1=Miyako meisho zue}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987|1=2002}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi|1=Musubi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816|1=1883}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048|1=604}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508|1=Hebizuka Kofun}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465|1=Akojidai}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|WD=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsanreimyo|1=Takamimusubi}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori|1=UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|lt=Torii|Q234731|WD=Q234731|1=Torii}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|lt=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|WD=Q843854|1=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden}} {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|WD=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine (Kyoto)}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176|WD=Q662176|1=Kitano Tenmangū}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yorishiro|1=UNKNOWN}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635|1=Narabigaoka}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828|1=Fushimi Inari-taisha}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{ill|lt=Christianity|Q5043|WD=Q5043|1=Christianity}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{ill|lt=Nestorian|Q168414|WD=Q168414|1=Nestorianism}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. . The current torii was rebuilt in {{ill|lt=Tenpo|Q1369045|WD=Q1369045|1=Tenpō}}2 years ({{ill|lt=1831|Q7579|WD=Q7579|1=1831}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}} years ({{ill|lt=1716|Q6892|WD=Q6892|1=1716}} - {{ill|lt=1735|Q6984|WD=Q6984|1=1735}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716|1=1780}}) ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495|1=Miyako meisho zue}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987|1=2002}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{ill|lt=Yamashiro Province|Q749276|WD=Q749276|1=Yamashiro Province}}, there are also {{ill|lt=Yamato Province|Q907495|WD=Q907495|1=Yamato Province}}, {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|WD=Q864163|1=Settsu Province}}, {{ill|lt=Tamba Province|Q954511|WD=Q954511|1=Tanba Province}}, {{ill|lt=Harima Province|Q1047523|WD=Q1047523|1=Harima Province}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} (King Ancestor God){{ill|lt=Ken Matsumae|Q11529297|WD=Q11529297|1=Takeshi Matsumae}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411|WD=Q10940411|1=Amenohoakari}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{ill|lt=Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|WD=Q11549157|1=Chiaki Mizutani}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496|WD=Q38278496|1=Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}・{{ill|lt=Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q11501968|WD=Q11501968|1=Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472|WD=Q11604472|1=Iibo Nimasu Amaterasu Shrine}}, {{ill|lt=There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|WD=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan|1=Tsushima Province}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. On the other hand, the direction of the {{ill|lt=three pillar torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}} in the grounds of Kijima Shrine is the winter solstice line of Mt. Inari and Mt. Matsuo, and the direction of Mt. Shimeidake and Mt. Atago. (Kyoto City)|Q2975204|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} is believed to be related to the summer solstice line of Mt. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi|1=Musubi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816|1=1883}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048|1=604}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508|1=Hebizuka Kofun}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465|1=Akojidai}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|WD=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsanreimyo|1=Takamimusubi}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|lt=Urabe|Q94724|WD=Q94724|1=Radical 25}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori|1=UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|lt=Torii|Q234731|WD=Q234731|1=Torii}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|lt=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|WD=Q843854|1=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden}} {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|WD=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine (Kyoto)}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176|WD=Q662176|1=Kitano Tenmangū}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{ill|lt=Yamashiro Province|Q749276|WD=Q749276|1=Yamashiro Province}}, there are also {{ill|lt=Yamato Province|Q907495|WD=Q907495|1=Yamato Province}}, {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|WD=Q864163|1=Settsu Province}}, {{ill|lt=Tamba Province|Q954511|WD=Q954511|1=Tanba Province}}, {{ill|lt=Harima Province|Q1047523|WD=Q1047523|1=Harima Province}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} (King Ancestor God){{ill|lt=Ken Matsumae|Q11529297|WD=Q11529297|1=Takeshi Matsumae}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411|WD=Q10940411|1=Amenohoakari}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{ill|lt=Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|WD=Q11549157|1=Chiaki Mizutani}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496|WD=Q38278496|1=Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}・{{ill|lt=Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q11501968|WD=Q11501968|1=Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472|WD=Q11604472|1=Iibo Nimasu Amaterasu Shrine}}, {{ill|lt=There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|WD=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan|1=Tsushima Province}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. On the other hand, the direction of the {{ill|lt=three pillar torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}} in the grounds of Kijima Shrine is the winter solstice line of Mt. Inari and Mt. Matsuo, and the direction of Mt. Shimeidake and Mt. Atago. (Kyoto City)|Q2975204|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} is believed to be related to the summer solstice line of Mt. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi|1=Musubi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816|1=1883}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048|1=604}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508|1=Hebizuka Kofun}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465|1=Akojidai}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|WD=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsanreimyo|1=Takamimusubi}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|lt=Urabe|Q94724|WD=Q94724|1=Radical 25}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|WD=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno. (Kyoto City)|Q11516217|WD=Q11516217|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine|1=Tsukiyomi Shrine (Kyoto)}} cannot be ignored. Meishin University It is listed at {{ill|lt=Meishin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} as ``Monthly Ainame Shinnai'' and is also held at the {{ill|lt=Monthly Festival|Q11516161|WD=Q11516161|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} and {{ill|lt=Ainamesai|Q11581944|WD=Q11581944|1=Ainame Festival}}・In {{ill|lt=Ninamesai|Q11501518|WD=Q11501518|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, it is written that it was kept in {{ill|lt=heihaku|Q11481885|WD=Q11481885|1=Hanpei}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. The company's name is pronounced as "Amaterasu Mimusuhi" in the Yoshida family book and "Amateru Mimusuhi" in the Kongoji book, but later in the ``{{ill|lt=Shinmyocho kosho|Q11588824|WD=Q11588824|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies}}''・In ``Jingishiryo'' and ``{{ill|lt=Shinja Roku|Q11590708|WD=Q11590708|1=Jinja Kakuroku}}'', it is called ``Amateru Mitama''{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In "Engishiki," Kijima Shrine is also mentioned in the Shijisai Shita Ainosaijo, the Extraordinary Festival Prayer Festival, and the Extraordinary Festival Meishinsaijo."Koryuji Raiyuki" which is {{ill|lt=Engage|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}} (Koryuji Raiyuki, Kaedeno Oigo, Kadeno Oigo, Kazuno District, Yamashiro Prefecture, established in {{ill|lt=Meio|Q1193841|WD=Q1193841|1=Meiō}} 8 ({{ill|lt=1499|Q6708|WD=Q6708|1=1499}})) [{{NDLDC|1879799/384}} "Gunshoju Shinkyo Volume 18"] (Naigai Publishing, 1931-1937, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 384-388 frames. In the Jogan era ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}} - In {{ill|lt=877|Q23905|WD=Q23905|1=877}}), the monk {{ill|lt=Dosho|Q11367403|WD=Q11367403|1=Dōshō}} performed blessings for rain at the pond of Kijima Meishin by imperial order, and was revered as the god of rain, so he was successively promoted to the divine rank. It is written that he reached the highest rank of Shoichii in {{ill|lt=Nagakyu|Q1193530|WD=Q1193530|1=Chōkyū}}4 ({{ill|lt=1043|Q19348|WD=Q19348|1=1043}}), and it is said that Kijima {{sub| {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}} "{{ill|lt=Ryojin Hisho|Q3010584|WD=Q3010584|1=Ryōjin Hishō}}", Kijima Shrine is {{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828|1=Fushimi Inari-taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Iwashimizu Hachimangu Shrine|Q710098|WD=Q710098|1=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}}, it is said to be a shrine that was constantly crowded with worshipers. {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.In {{ill|lt=Jokyu War|Q1372308|WD=Q1372308|1=Jōkyū War}} of {{ill|lt=Jokyu|Q1195428|WD=Q1195428|1=Jōkyū}} 3rd year ({{ill|lt=1221|Q5393|WD=Q5393|1=1221}}) of {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|WD=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}, "{{ill|lt=Azuma Kagami|Q1042324|WD=Q1042324|1=Azuma Kagami}}" Azuma Kagami article dated June 15, 1221. In , it appears that {{ill|lt=Emperor Gotoba|Q316658|WD=Q316658|lt=Retired Emperor Gotoba|1=Emperor Go-Toba}}'s {{ill|lt=Taneyoshi Miura|Q11356551|WD=Q11356551|1=Miura Taneyoshi}} and his children Tanenren and Kaneyoshi committed suicide at ``Nishiyama Kijima'', but this is believed to be the place {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. According to ``{{ill|lt=Jōkyūki|Q11497315|WD=Q11497315|1=Jōkyūki}}'', Taneyoshi was hiding in ``Konojima Shrine'', but when he realized his fate, he committed suicide, and Rojo set the shrine on fire {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Recent excavations within the shrine grounds have revealed traces of land leveling in the early Kamakura period, which appears to have been done during the rebuilding of the shrine building after it was destroyed by fire.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} After that, it is not mentioned in literature until around {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, and its history is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716|1=1780}})'s ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495|1=Miyako meisho zue}}'' depicts the precincts at that time {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.After {{ill|lt=Meiji Restoration|Q8707|WD=Q8707|1=Meiji Restoration}}, in June {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|WD=Q7757|1=1873}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}6) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{ill|lt=Gosha|Q134917316|WD=Q134917316|1=Gō-sha}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. In {{ill|lt=1985|Q2431|WD=Q2431|1=1985}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}60), the precincts were designated as a designated historic site by Kyoto City . In {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987|1=2002}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}14), an excavation survey was conducted for the first time as a historic site in conjunction with the installation of a fire tank in the northeast corner of the precincts.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. === God level === * Record of {{ill|lt=Divine rank|Q11591025|WD=Q11591025|1=Shinkai (divine rank)}} dedication during the Six Kingdoms historical period ** {{ill|lt=Ten'an (Japan)|Q1075611|WD=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an|1=Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{ill|lt=859|Q23897|WD=Q23897|1=859}}), from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Sei Fifth Rank Lower ("{{ill|lt=Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}") "Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku" Article dated 27th New Year, Jogan 1st year (859) (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). - The notation is "Kijima Amaterasu Mitama-kami." * After Six Kingdoms History ** {{ill|lt=Johei (Japan)|Q1324874|WD=Q1324874|lt=Johei|1=Jōhei}} October 23, 6th year ({{ill|lt=936|Q23584|WD=Q23584|1=936}}), from upper fifth rank to lower rank of junior fourth rank (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** October 28, {{ill|lt=Nagayasu|Q1324844|WD=Q1324844|1=Chōhō (era)}}5th year ({{ill|lt=1003|Q19224|WD=Q19224|1=1003}}), Junichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) ** May 10th, {{ill|lt=Nagakyu|Q1193530|WD=Q1193530|1=Chōkyū}}4th year ({{ill|lt=1043|Q19348|WD=Q19348|1=1043}}), Shoichii (Koryuji Raiyuki) === Precincts === [[File:Konoshima-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (left) and Seriyo Shrine (right)}}]] The precincts are located at the eastern end of the low terrace on the right bank of the Omuro River, just south of {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635|1=Narabigaoka}} (Futagaoka) and just east of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori|1=UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|lt=Torii|Q234731|WD=Q234731|1=Torii}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|lt=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|WD=Q843854|1=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden}} {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|WD=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine (Kyoto)}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176|WD=Q662176|1=Kitano Tenmangū}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yorishiro|1=UNKNOWN}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635|1=Narabigaoka}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828|1=Fushimi Inari-taisha}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{ill|lt=Christianity|Q5043|WD=Q5043|1=Christianity}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{ill|lt=Nestorian|Q168414|WD=Q168414|1=Nestorianism}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. . The current torii was rebuilt in {{ill|lt=Tenpo|Q1369045|WD=Q1369045|1=Tenpō}}2 years ({{ill|lt=1831|Q7579|WD=Q7579|1=1831}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}} years ({{ill|lt=1716|Q6892|WD=Q6892|1=1716}} - {{ill|lt=1735|Q6984|WD=Q6984|1=1735}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716|1=1780}}) ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495|1=Miyako meisho zue}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987|1=2002}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. The common name of Kijima Shrine, ``Silkworm Shrine,'' originates from this Seriyo Shrine. * Akina Shrine *: Enshrined deity: Mitsui Takayasu ({{ill|lt=Mitsui family|Q950465|WD=Q950465|1=Mitsui family}} distant ancestor) {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}} * Inari Shrine * Ryodo Shrine * Konchin Shrine * Misono Inari Shrine * Yasaka Shrine *Shokukuni Shrine * Tenma Shrine * Sanjuhachisho Shrine * Hakusei Shrine * Hakutoku Shrine * Hashihime Shrine * Tsubakioka Shrine === Cultural assets === === Kyoto City designated historic site === * Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts - Designated June 1, 1985 [http://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/bunshi/page/0000005897.html Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Property -Historic Site- Ukyo Ward] (Kyoto City Home Page). . === Appeared works === * 2 poems from “{{ill|lt=Ryojin Hisho|Q3010584|WD=Q3010584|1=Ryōjin Hishō}}” Volume 2 {{Cquote|Kane no Mitake is one place in the world, Kongo Zao Shaka Miroku, Inari, Yawata, Kijima, etc. There is no time when no one visits.
"New Edition of Japanese Classical Literature Complete Works 42 Kagura Uta/Jimagaku/Ryojin Hisho/Kanginshu" Shogakukan, 2000 (Japan Knowledge Edition), p. 254. }} {{Cquote|The medicine man of Uzumasa keeps staying with Maro as he goes to his home.'''The God of Kijima''
　{{small|Note) The medicine man of Uzumasa: Is it the Medicine Buddha of {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}?}}|20px||``Ryojin Hisho'' Volume 2 Two-Phrase Divine Poem Shrine Songs (No. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|WD=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi|1=Musubi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|WD=Q7816|1=1883}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|WD=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|WD=Q31048|1=604}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|WD=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|WD=Q11625508|1=Hebizuka Kofun}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|WD=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|WD=Q57538465|1=Akojidai}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|WD=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsanreimyo|1=Takamimusubi}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|WD=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} 1st year ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|WD=Q23496|1=701}}) , making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|WD=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). .All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship. [[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|lt=Three Pillar Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}}}]] In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori|1=UNKNOWN}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|lt=Three-Pillared Torii|Q3532297|WD=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|lt=Torii|Q234731|WD=Q234731|1=Torii}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto""Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|lt=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|WD=Q843854|1=Kyoto Gyoen National Garden}} {{ill|lt=Itsukushima Shrine (Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City)|Q11410134|WD=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine|1=Itsukushima Shrine (Kyoto)}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|Q662176|WD=Q662176|1=Kitano Tenmangū}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. . The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yorishiro|1=UNKNOWN}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{ill|lt=Futagaoka|Q18337635|WD=Q18337635|1=Narabigaoka}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|WD=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{ill|lt=Fushimi Inari Taisha|Q714828|WD=Q714828|1=Fushimi Inari-taisha}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{ill|lt=Christianity|Q5043|WD=Q5043|1=Christianity}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{ill|lt=Nestorian|Q168414|WD=Q168414|1=Nestorianism}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. . The current torii was rebuilt in {{ill|lt=Tenpo|Q1369045|WD=Q1369045|1=Tenpō}}2 years ({{ill|lt=1831|Q7579|WD=Q7579|1=1831}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{ill|lt=Kyoho|Q1145048|WD=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}} years ({{ill|lt=1716|Q6892|WD=Q6892|1=1716}} - {{ill|lt=1735|Q6984|WD=Q6984|1=1735}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}}9 ({{ill|lt=1780|Q7716|WD=Q7716|1=1780}}) ``{{ill|lt=Capital Meisho Zue|Q11643495|WD=Q11643495|1=Miyako meisho zue}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{ill|lt=2002|Q1987|WD=Q1987|1=2002}} ({{ill|lt=Heisei|Q234510|WD=Q234510|1=Heisei era}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}} * Main shrine - Rebuilt in the {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} era. * Place of worship - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Worship Hall - Rebuilt during the Meiji era. * Motadasu Pond * Three pillar torii * Jinko * Shrine office File:Konoshima-jinja torii.JPG|Torii File:Konoshima-jinja haiden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Kaiko-yashiro Kijima Shrine Honden-mae.jpg|In front of the main hall === Setsusha === The following shrines are enshrined within the shrine grounds: {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. * Kogai Shrine *: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto *: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. It is also commonly known as ``Konoshima Shrine'' (Konoshima Shrine) and ``Kaikono Yashiro'' (Silkworm Shrine). This shrine has long been worshiped as the god of prayers for rain, and is known for having a rare {{ill|lt=three-pillar torii|Q3532297|qid=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}} within its grounds. === Enshrined God === The following five deities are enshrined. . :* {{ill|lt=Amenominakanushikami|Q2842779|qid=Q2842779|1=Ame-no-Minakanushi}} :* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Okuni Tamakami|1=UNKNOWN}} :* {{ill|lt=Hoori|Q1051960|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hodemi Mikoto|1=Hoori}} :* {{ill|lt=Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|qid=Q1373935|lt=Ugayafukiaezu Mikoto|1=Ugayafukiaezu}} :* {{ill|lt=Ninigi|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Keorigi no Mikoto|1=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}} (Ninigi no Mikoto) {{Location map+|Japan|width=220|float=right|caption={{Center|Distribution of Amaterasu Mitama Shrine, Amaterasu Shrine, and

In the same book, it is listed as ``Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine,'' but since this name means ``the shrine of the Amaterasu Mitama deity enshrined in Kijima (place name),'' it was originally a shrine dedicated to ``Amateru Mitama no Kami.'' In addition to Kijima Shrine in {{ill|lt=Yamashiro Province|Q749276|qid=Q749276|1=Yamashiro Province}}, there are also {{ill|lt=Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495|1=Yamato Province}}, {{ill|lt=Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163|1=Settsu Province}}, {{ill|lt=Tamba Province|Q954511|qid=Q954511|1=Tanba Province}}, {{ill|lt=Harima Province|Q1047523|qid=Q1047523|1=Harima Province}}, { There are shrines dedicated to Amaterasu Mitama, Amaterasu, and Amaterasu Tamakami in places such as {jalink|Tsushima Country|Q1054861}}, but these are thought to be sun gods with a different deity from {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|qid=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}} (King Ancestor God){{ill|lt=Ken Matsumae|Q11529297|qid=Q11529297|1=Takeshi Matsumae}} “A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. .Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Amenka Mei-no-Mikoto|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411|1=Amenohoakari}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, the local rituals were inherited.{{ill|lt=Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|qid=Q11549157|1=Chiaki Mizutani}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. . Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}・{{ill|lt=Kagamiza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q38278496|qid=Q38278496|1=Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}・{{ill|lt=Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|Q11501968|qid=Q11501968|1=Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Tokuza Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472|qid=Q11604472|1=Iibo Nimasu Amaterasu Shrine}}, {{ill|lt=There is one shrine that is believed to have been worshiped by the Tsushima clan|Q1054861|qid=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan|1=Tsushima Province}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. On the other hand, the direction of the {{ill|lt=three pillar torii|Q3532297|qid=Q3532297|1=Mihashira Torii}} in the grounds of Kijima Shrine is the winter solstice line of Mt. Inari and Mt. Matsuo, and the direction of Mt. Shimeidake and Mt. Atago. (Kyoto City)|Q2975204|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} is believed to be related to the summer solstice line of Mt. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|lt=Musuhi|Q11279555|qid=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi|1=Musubi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|lt=1883|Q7816|qid=Q7816|1=1883}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}. === History === === Founding === Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|lt=Emperor Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057|1=Empress Suiko}}12 ({{ill|lt=604|Q31048|qid=Q31048|1=604}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested|1=UNKNOWN}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|lt=Taiho (Japan)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho|1=Taihō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=701|Q23496|qid=Q23496|1=701}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|lt=#enshrined deity|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|lt=Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290|1=Hata clan}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|lt=Koryuji|Q3076920|qid=Q3076920|1=Kōryū-ji}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|lt=Matsuo Taisha|Q710302|qid=Q710302|1=Matsunoo Taisha}} and {{ill|lt=Jabizuka Tumulus|Q11625508|qid=Q11625508|1=Hebizuka Kofun}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|lt=Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858|1=Yayoi period}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo|1=UNKNOWN}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|lt=Akojidai|Q57538465|qid=Q57538465|1=Akojidai}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsanreimyo|1=Takamimusubi}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|lt=Urabe|Q94724|qid=Q94724|1=Radical 25}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|lt=Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311|1=Owari clan}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine in Kazuno. (Kyoto City)|Q11516217|qid=Q11516217|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine|1=Tsukiyomi Shrine (Kyoto)}} cannot be ignored.
